_comment: COS212 Quiz — fresh BST and DFS application scenarios. Eight questions per attempt, with A/B variants.

items.prompt: Where should you insert 81 in Tree A?

options.feedback: Correct: 81 > 67, 81 < 86, then 81 > 74. The right child of 74 is empty.
81 is greater than 74, so it must be to its right.
81 is smaller than 86, so move left, not right.
81 is greater than the root 67, so it belongs in the right subtree.

items.prompt: Where should you insert 79 in Tree B?

options.feedback: Correct: 79 > 59, 79 < 82, then 79 > 72. Insert to the right of 72.
79 is larger than 72, so it cannot go left of 72.
79 is larger than the root 59. It belongs in the right subtree.
79 is smaller than 82, so follow the left child of 82.

items.prompt: Why would moving node 74 anywhere into the left subtree of 67 break the BST rule?

options.feedback: Correct. Every value in the left subtree of 67 must be smaller than 67.
Check the comparison: 74 is greater than 67.

options.text: A left subtree can only contain one node
options.feedback: A BST subtree may contain many nodes if each placement follows its ancestor constraints.
Whether a node is a leaf does not determine which side of the root it belongs on.

items.prompt: Why would placing node 36 anywhere in the right subtree of 59 break the BST rule?

options.feedback: Correct. All values in the right subtree of 59 must be greater than 59.
36 is smaller than 59, not larger.

options.text: The right subtree must contain only leaves
options.feedback: Internal nodes are allowed anywhere their BST ordering constraints are satisfied.
The root is 59. Node 36 can belong to its left subtree.

items.prompt: DFS visits 67 and pushes its right child 86, then left child 33. Which node is on top of the stack?

options.feedback: Correct. The last node pushed, 33, is popped next.
86 was pushed before 33, so it sits below 33.
67 was already popped and visited, so it is no longer on the stack.
15 has not been pushed yet; DFS must first visit 33.

items.prompt: After visiting 82, DFS pushes 93 and then 72. Which value is popped next?

options.feedback: Correct. Left-first DFS pushes the right child first, then the left child on top.
93 was pushed first, so 72 is above it in the LIFO stack.
82 has already been popped and visited.
59 is the root and was visited earlier.

items.prompt: In left-first Pre-order DFS on Tree A, node 15 has just been visited. Click the node DFS visits next.

options.feedback: Correct. 15 is a leaf. DFS backtracks to the waiting right branch of 33 and visits 52.
33 was already visited. DFS continues from its pending right branch.
The left subtree of 67 still has node 52 waiting.
DFS first visits parent 52 before entering its left child 45.

items.prompt: In left-first Pre-order DFS on Tree B, node 13 has just been visited. Click the node DFS visits next.

options.feedback: Correct. After leaf 13, DFS resumes at the pending right child of 26, node 41.
26 has already been visited. DFS continues with its pending right branch.
DFS completes the left subtree of 59 before moving to node 82.
The next visit is parent 41. Its child 36 is visited afterward.

items.prompt: How many nodes does left-first Pre-order DFS visit before finding 96 in Tree A?

options.feedback: Correct. DFS visits 67 → 33 → 15 → 52 → 45 → 86 → 74 → 96, including the target.
That counts the BST lookup path, not left-first DFS. DFS explores the left subtree first.
Remember to count the final visit to target 96.
DFS also visits nodes in the right subtree before reaching 96.

items.prompt: How many nodes does left-first Pre-order DFS visit before finding 72 in Tree B?

options.feedback: Correct. DFS visits 59 → 26 → 13 → 41 → 36 → 82 → 72, and stops at the target.
That is the BST lookup path (59 → 82 → 72), not a full left-first DFS search.
DFS stops when it finds 72, so it does not visit 93 afterward.
The visit to 82 and then 72 also count toward the total.

items.prompt: Build the full Pre-order traversal for Tree A.
items.correctFeedback: Correct. Pre-order follows Root → Left → Right.

rules.feedback: That looks like In-order. Recheck where the parent is visited.

items.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Check position {position}; it should be {expected}. Reapply the Pre-order rule at every subtree.
